Definition: from G5259 and G435; in subjection under a man, i.e. a married woman:--which hath an husband.
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, hýpandros is the word for under a husband, married. In Romans 7:2, the text says "For the woman which hath an husband is bound by the law to [her] husband so long as he liveth."
TheologicalSignificance: In hýpandros I find no hidden theology; it simply means under a husband, married.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
